articles.title: Sabalenka gana a Muchova y Andreeva a Svitolina en las Finales WTA
articles.standfirst: Superaron a la checa Karolina Muchova y a la ucraniana Elena Svitolina, respectivamente
articles.summary: Superaron a la checa Karolina Muchova y a la ucraniana Elena Svitolina, respectivamente
articles.body: La bielorrusa Aryna Sabalenka y la rusa Mirra Andreeva superaron a la checa Karolina Muchova y a la ucraniana Elena Svitolina, respectivamente, en su debut en las Finales de la WTA en 2026 que se disputan en Indian Wells. Sabalenka, número dos del mundo, se deshizo de Muchova (n.7) por 7-6(2) y 7-5 en 1 hora y 53 minutos. La bielorrusa, que perdió el número uno en septiembre tras casi dos años, nunca ha ganado unas Finales de la WTA. Por su lado, Andreeva, vigente campeona en Roland Garros, derrotó a Svitolina por 6-4 y 6-0 en solo 1 hora y 10 minutos. Para Svitolina, este fue su primer partido desde que anunció su separación del francés Gael Monfils, su esposo. Andreeva y Sabalenka encabezan ahora el Grupo 2 de las Finales de la WTA, que reúne a las ocho mejores tenistas del año, a la conclusión de la primera jornada. Este martes arranca la segunda jornada con los partidos del Grupo 1 entre la estadounidense Coco Gauff y la checa Linda Noskova y entre la también estadounidense Jessica Pegula y la ucraniana Marta Kostyuk. Noskova y Gauff lideran ese grupo tras sus respectivas victorias del domingo ante Kostyuk y Pegula.

articles.title: Sinner: "El objetivo es volver en Australia, pero tengo que ir paso a paso"
articles.standfirst: El italiano concede una rueda de prensa en Milán y reconoce que "por primera vez en mi carrera, no tengo control sobre las cosas"
articles.summary: El italiano habla para La Gazzetta sobre su tratamiento en la rodilla,
articles.body: Jannik Sinner, apartado de las pistas desde el 12 de julio por una lesión en la rodilla derecha, ha concedido una rueda de prensa en Milán para tratar su situación actual con el tratamiento conservador y cómo es la vida fuera del circuito. También le ha acompañado su ya exentrenador, Darren Cahill, con el que anunció su separación profesional hace tan solo cuatro días y para el que siempre tiene buenas palabras: "Darren tiene mucha experiencia. Ha vivido momentos en la pista antes que yo y me ha ayudado mucho a lo largo de estos años". No son tiempos fáciles para Jannik, con cinco Masters 1000 y un grande a sus espaldas, tuvo que verse obligado a despedirse de la temporada para centrarse en su rodilla derecha: "No son meses fáciles, echo de menos la competición y dar el 100%. Si volviera a la pista un mes después, nada cambiaría. Quiero jugar otros 10 o 15 años más. Fue un año interesante. Gané Wimbledon y Roma, lo que me dio una alegría enorme, pero ahora tengo que centrarme en seguir los tratamientos", empieza el italiano. También ha mencionado la presión que siente por volver: "Siento un poco la presión, no puedo evitarlo. Teníamos un objetivo en mente, China, y tuvimos que cambiar las cosas sobre la marcha. Tengo que hacer caso a lo que me dicen los médicos". El transalpino ha querido marcar su gran objetivo: "El objetivo es volver en Australia. Quizás jugar algunos torneos antes, pero tengo que ir paso a paso hacia ese objetivo, porque si nos precipitamos, las cosas podrían empeorar. Pero el objetivo es Australia", aclara. Sobre si continúa viendo tenis aun estando fuera: "No veía mucho porque yo también quería estar allí. Antes, jugar un torneo y ganarlo me parecía lo más normal del mundo. Ahora que lo echo de menos, valoro aún más lo que he logrado. Seguiré viviendo el tenis de la misma manera, con amor y pasión, porque tengo la suerte de haberlo elegido como profesión", ha querido añadir el campeón de cinco grandes. Aunque los días, según cuenta, se le están haciendo largos al tenista de San Cándido: "Por primera vez en mi carrera, no tengo control sobre las cosas. Es un momento difícil porque voy del simulador al gimnasio y luego al simulador... Viajo un poco, visito a amigos y luego a mis padres. Así que estoy viviendo algo que nunca antes había experimentado. No tengo el control de la situación. Esta es quizás la parte más difícil de este período, pero solo tengo que ser paciente y confiar", cierra Jannik Sinner.

articles.title: Jannik Sinner: World No 2 confirms aim to return to tennis at Australian Open after lengthy absence with knee injury
articles.summary: Jannik Sinner has confirmed his plans to return from injury at the Australian Open in January; The World No 2 has not played since July and recently lost the top spot in the rankings to Alexander Zverev; watch the WTA Finals this week, live on Sky Sports Tennis
articles.body:
The Italian has not played since defending his Wimbledon title in July due to a knee injury.

Sinner, who has lost his world number one spot to Alexander Zverev, won the Melbourne title in 2024 and 2025 but was beaten by Novak Djokovic in this year's semi-final.

"The goal is to return to Australia," the 25-year-old said at press conference in Milan.

"Maybe play a few tournaments earlier. But I have to take everything one step after the other every day towards the goal because if we hurry then maybe it will be worse. But yes, the goal is Australia"

The five-time Grand Slam winner also lauded Brit Jack Draper alongside Matteo Berrettini and Carlos Alcaraz for his support during his period out with injury.

Draper himself has ruled out returning before 2027 after missing every Grand Slam this year, and said he was in a "difficult place" after his first-round defeat by Martin Landaluce in the Cincinnati Open in August, admitting he was struggling to escape the mental fatigue that had built up during 15 months of battling serious injury.

"When I announced that my season was over, Berrettini and Draper got in touch straight away," Sinner added. "Jack is also going through a difficult period, so he understands what I'm going through.

"Alcaraz had sent me a message, just as I message him. I really appreciated it.

"We are trying to find a way out of this situation and working towards experiencing those emotions again.

"For me, tennis is not a job. I continue to play because I enjoy it."

Alongside detailing his rehabilitation process, Sinner extended his congratulations to fellow Italian Kimi Antonelli after the 20-year-old became the youngest ever Formula 1 World Champion after finishing third at the Mexico City Grand Prix .

"Motorsport is the only sport I watch that gets me excited. When I watch MotoGP and Formula 1, it gives me an incredible boost.

"Kimi has done something incredible. He's learned so much this year, and what he's done moves me deeply.

"He's a completely normal, very laid-back guy, and this shows the most normal side of a 20-year-old, which is what we have most in common."

articles.title: La gesta de Pliskova: ganar 1.002 puestos tras 'reaprender' a caminar
articles.standfirst: La checa, que empezó la temporada como la 1.054 y la acabará entre las 60 primeras, protagoniza la mayor subida de posiciones en la WTA de la temporada 2026
articles.summary: La checa, que empezó la temporada como la 1.054 y la acabará entre las 60 primeras, protagoniza la mayor subida de posiciones en la WTA de la temporada 2026
articles.body: Karolina Pliskova, la que en 2017 fuera reina del circuito femenino, ha protagonizado la mayor subida de posiciones en el ranking WTA de la presente temporada. La checa comenzaba la semana del 5 de enero como la 1.054 en las listas. A día 10 de noviembre firma la posición 52, protagonizando un ascenso de 1.002 escalones. En el US Open 2024, mientras disputaba su partido de segunda ronda ante Jasmine Paolini, Pliskova sufrió una rotura de los ligamentos del tobillo izquierdo tras una caída en el tercer punto del encuentro. Siempre alardeaba de su capacidad para jugar a pesar del dolor y que nunca se retiraría de un partido, a no ser que la situación fuera realmente grave. Aquella vez, lo era. "Se te olvida cómo caminar, pierdes toda la musculatura, toda la movilidad. Y el tobillo es un problema porque todo el cuerpo recae sobre él. Tienes que empezar a usarlo de nuevo poco a poco", declaraba Pliskova durante el pasado mes de junio en el torneo de Queens. La bota ortopédica que llegó a portar por seis meses no le permitía ni pisar el suelo. Se complicó aún más cuando tuvo que volver a pasar por el quirófano tras una infección en la zona, lo que la obligó a estar dos meses más sin apoyar. Un año de sufrimiento e incertidumbre. Por aquel entonces, la que era 44 del mundo, pasó a ser la 1.056. En el presente curso, la checa ha demostrado que vuelve a ser competitiva. Los cuartos de final alcanzados en Madrid o las semifinales en Nottingham han ayudado a la gran subida de la campeona de 17 títulos WTA. Más de 1.000 posiciones después, se encuentra entre las 60 mejores raquetas femeninas (52), justo donde la lesión la obligó a parar hace dos años.

articles.title: Jannik Sinner targets late-December comeback, keeps Australian Open 2027 in focus
articles.summary: Jannik Sinner is targeting a return to competitive tennis in late December as he steps up his recovery from a persistent knee injury, with the Six Kings
articles.body: Jannik Sinner is targeting a return to competitive tennis in late December as he steps up his recovery from a persistent knee injury, with the Six Kings Slam in Saudi Arabia emerging as a possible first stop ahead of the 2027 Australian Open.The Italian, who has been sidelined since winning the Wimbledon title in July, offered an update on his recovery at a event in Milan on Tuesday. While he is keen to return to the court before the new season, Sinner made it clear that he will not rush the process at the risk of aggravating his injury."The aim is to go to Australia, the aim is also maybe to do a couple of tournaments first. But I have to respect the protocols at the moment because if we rush things we could have more serious problems," Sinner said."I also only have that information, that I have to work hard every day for that objective and then we'll see."Six Kings Slam could mark Sinner's returnThe rescheduled Six Kings Slam in Riyadh is among the events Sinner is targeting as he looks to regain match fitness before the Australian Open. The exhibition tournament, which was initially scheduled for October, has been moved to December 27-30 amid security concerns in the Middle East. Sinner acknowledged that the event remains a possibility rather than a certainty, with the wider situation in the region also playing a part in the decision."That (is the target) but we all know the situation what's there at the moment, which is not the best, so this is not our decision as players, this is a more general decision," he said.The Italian added that playing some matches before travelling to Australia could be beneficial, given that he has not competed since Wimbledon."But I think if we want to prepare for Australia (and) I'm not playing since Wimbledon, some matches before might be very helpful," he added.The Six Kings Slam does not offer ATP ranking points but brings together some of the biggest names in men's tennis. Sinner won the previous edition and is expected to feature alongside Carlos Alcaraz, Novak Djokovic, Alexander Zverev, Taylor Fritz and Alex de Minaur.Knee injury ended Sinner's 2026 season earlySinner's last appearance came in the Wimbledon final in July, where he defeated Alexander Zverev to claim the fifth Grand Slam title of his career. However, a right knee problem subsequently forced him to miss several tournaments, including the US Open.The prolonged recovery eventually led the 25-year-old to announce in October that he would not compete again in the 2026 ATP season. His extended absence also saw him lose the world No. 1 ranking, with Zverev taking over the top spot last week after Sinner's 95-week reign.Sinner has reiterated that his priority is to return fully fit rather than risk a setback by making an early comeback. With the Australian Open scheduled for January, the late-December target could offer him an opportunity to get valuable match practice before the first Grand Slam of 2027.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: “Choose wisely”: Andre Agassi opens up on finding lasting love with Steffi Graf after going through a failed marriage
articles.summary: Andre Agassi, the tennis legend, has been public about the traumatic and painful childhood he went through as his father trained him intensely.
articles.body: Andre Agassi, the tennis legend, has been public about the traumatic and painful childhood he went through as his father trained him intensely. While that has been a dark chapter in Andre Agassi’s career, one thing he has always taken pride in is his high profile marriage to fellow tennis champion, Steffi Graf. After over two decades of being together, Andre Agassi opens up on choosing a life partner.Andre Agassi reflects on what's important in marriage as his bond with Steffi Graf inspires millionsIn an interview with E! News, the tennis legend Andre Agassi reflected on the secret behind a long lasting and happy marriage as he joked, "Choose wisely," before adding, "No, I mean, I think it's like success in life or in anything you do. I think there's a determination you have to be in the most of yourself, in balance of the most of what somebody needs from you, giving what it is you have to give and not attempting to give what you don't.”Andre Agassi added, “But not leaving anything in the tank when you can give it right."The tennis legend also reflected on how he and Steffi Graf have remained best friends for over two decades as he continued, "We love cooking together," Andre added. "We love hiking together. We love even grocery shopping together, dividing and conquering. So it's real life. And we're blessed."In the last two decades, Andre Agassi and Steffi Graf have quickly turned into one of the most inspiring couples. Both of them have remained pretty protective about their two children, Jaden, 22, and Jaz, 20, as they have publicly spoken of how there is no pressure on them to choose a career in tennis or professional sports.However, life was not always this perfect for Andre Agassi. Before he met and fell in love with Steffi Graf, he was married to popular actress Brooke Shields.Andre Agassi experienced a painful divorce before he fell for Steffi GrafWhile Andre Agassi and Brooke Shields dared each other for a few years before tying the knot, things did not work out well between them.With Andre Agassi’s busy career, the two hardly found any time to spend together and this created a lot of emotional distance between them. To make it worse, there had also been many infidelity rumors surrounding their high profile marriage.Just two years after tying the knot, Andre Agassi and Steffi Graf went their separate ways in 1999.Two years later, Andre Agassi and Steffi Graf tied the knot in 2001 and the rest was history. The two continue to remain happily married as they have put their focus on raising their two children out of the spotlight.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.
